% Pattern: head/case. "The case" heads a case as "Case" does, as {\it The
% case $1\le |x|\le |y|$}., even when the formula starts with a digit; and
% formulas that "and" joins name a case, as {\bf Case $s \neq 1$ and
% $K=K_0$.}. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-1 other/case -
% want head-2 other/case -
% want head-3 other/case -
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem}
Every set is small.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
{\it The case $1\le |x|\le |y|$}. Let us show that it holds.

{\it The case $|x|\le 1$.} Then it holds.

{\bf Case $s \neq 1$ and $K=K_0$.} Then it holds too.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
